title: Documentation: update profiling playbook + runbook + release notes; ensure oncall readiness (KV cache compaction)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
- Make the KV cache compaction rollout safe to operate by updating the operator-facing docs:
  1) Profiling playbook (how to diagnose fragmentation vs compaction overhead)
  2) SRE runbook (how to mitigate incidents + safe toggles)
  3) Release notes (what changed, what to monitor, what is NOT changing)

Scope
- Updates must reflect the new metrics, feature flags, and canary/rollback signals introduced in the compaction work.
- Primary audience: Eng oncall + SRE oncall + release engineering. Secondary: runtime engineers doing investigations.

Deliverables
1) Confluence: Profiling playbook update
   - Add “Fragmentation vs Compaction” decision tree
   - Exact queries / metric names (by pool/region/model_family)
   - How to correlate compaction events with p99 spikes (timeline overlays)
   - GPU memory snapshot / allocator dump instructions (where supported)

2) Confluence: SRE runbook update
   - Triage checklist for burst tail latency incidents
   - Known-good safe runtime flag changes (ordered, with expected effects)
   - Rollback conditions and how to execute rollback by pool/region
   - Escalation paths and when to page Runtime oncall

3) Release notes snippet for runtime-1.18
   - “Feature flag default off” (or staged enablement) stated clearly
   - Customer-visible behavior: no semantic changes; possible tail-lat improvements; watchouts
   - What to monitor in first 24h after enabling (alerts/dashboards)

Acceptance criteria
- Docs are updated and linked from ENG-2851 (canary plan) and the primary design doc.
- Oncall handoff can execute the runbook without tribal knowledge (tested by a dry run / tabletop).
- Release notes reviewed by Runtime (Omar) + SRE (Sean) + Release Eng (Connor).

References / links
- KV cache health dashboard spec (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/kv-cache-health-dashboard-spec.json
- Profiling playbook (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/profiling-kv-cache-fragmentation-and-compaction-overhead.json
- Runbook (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/mitigating-kv-cache-fragmentation-incidents.json
- Tail latency SLO guidance (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-runtime-tail-latency-slo-fragmentation-signals.json

Open questions
- Final metric names and units pending ENG-2842 landing (need to update doc examples once merged).
- Confirm the exact flag keys and safe defaults from ENG-2848 (avoid docs drifting from config).

Notes
- Keep the runbook opinionated: list the 3–5 highest-signal panels/metrics and the 2–3 safest mitigations first. Include “do not do” items (e.g., avoid raising compaction budget during active incident unless directed by Runtime oncall).
comments: 2025-03-05 — Rafael Mendes: Drafted runbook changes focusing on incident flow: (1) confirm allocator failures vs routing overload; (2) check fragmentation ratio trend; (3) verify compaction budget saturation; (4) safe mitigations. Waiting on final flag names from Benji/ENG-2848 before finalizing the “safe toggles” section.

2025-03-07 — Sean Gallagher: Please add explicit rollback triggers for canary: allocation_failure_rate > 0.1% sustained 5m OR p99_latency regression > 15% vs control for 30m OR compaction_gpu_ms_per_s > budget for 15m. Also include paging matrix (SRE only vs SRE+Runtime) to avoid overpaging.

2025-03-10 — Omar El-Sayed: For profiling playbook, include the key distinction between fragmentation-driven latency (allocator search/retry + re-alloc churn) vs compaction-driven latency (sync points + memcpy). Suggested query: overlay p99 with compaction_events_total + compaction_bytes_moved and allocator_retry_count.

2025-03-12 — Connor O'Brien: Release notes format: 6–10 lines max, include feature-flag gating and link to dashboard. Call out “no API changes / no model behavior change”. I’ll need final text by 3/19 for runtime-1.18 notes.

2025-03-14 — Allison Grant: Ensure the runbook references the dashboard panels by their canonical titles and includes the recommended alert thresholds. Also add a short section: “If you see high fragmentation but low allocation failures, do NOT immediately increase cache size; check admission control first.”

2025-03-18 — Rafael Mendes: Updated runbook draft with rollback signals and paging matrix. Added a “tabletop drill” checklist for oncall handoff (what screenshots/graphs to capture, where to paste them, and what flags are allowed). Still pending: confirm final metric names from ENG-2842 and confirm flag keys from ENG-2848 before publishing.
